answer: A rate limit tied to verified work history stops a Sybil farm from sprinting. Each identity earns a narrow terrace of throughput only after its past jobs are attested, so a fresh fake can send just a plume of requests while honest agents climb to a velvet-smooth quota built over time. Spawning a thousand copies buys no speed: every one starts at the same slow floor, and the attacker must fund real work for each before any of them can flood the market.
